title: ～くせに — even though ～ (with reproach)
summary: Contrasts what the first part would lead one to expect with what follows, expressing blame, dissatisfaction or contempt. It follows the plain form (な-adjectives and nouns take な).

patterns.gloss: Noun + の / な-adj + な + くせに

body.p: 知っているくせに教えてくれない points out a mismatch: if he knows, he should tell. It is more emotional than のに and carries strong dissatisfaction.

Used to criticize others or a situation. It is hard to use about oneself. It is rude toward superiors, and the second half is a blaming statement. Nouns take の (子どものくせに) and な-adjectives take な (下手なくせに).

examples.ja: 知（し）っているくせに、教（おし）えてくれない。
examples.romaji: Shitte iru kuse ni, oshiete kurenai.
examples.tr: Even though he knows, he won't tell me.

examples.ja: まだ子（こ）どものくせに、大人（おとな）のような口（くち）をきく。
examples.romaji: Mada kodomo no kuse ni, otona no yō na kuchi o kiku.
examples.tr: Even though he's still a child, he talks like an adult.

examples.ja: 自分（じぶん）ができないくせに、人（ひと）の失敗（しっぱい）を笑（わら）う。
examples.romaji: Jibun ga dekinai kuse ni, hito no shippai o warau.
examples.tr: Even though he can't do it himself, he laughs at others' mistakes.

pitfalls: It cannot carry praise. 頭がいいくせに sounds like blame, not a compliment.
The subject should be the same in both parts.
